title: The Who NYC: Tickets Under $100 for 2 Shows
text:
The Who Announces Final US Tour with New York Stops, Tickets Starting Under $100 A final chance to experience the iconic rock band The Who is on the horizon, as they embark on what they’ve declared will be their last tour of the United States, including two New York performances.
Legendary British rock band The Who will bring their “The Song Is Over Farewell Tour” to the Northwell at Jones Beach Theater in Wantagh, New York, on August 28, followed by a performance at Madison Square Garden on August 30. This tour marks what the band insists will be their last run of shows across the country.
Finding the Cheapest Tickets
For fans eager to witness this historic tour, affordable tickets are still available. According to a recent search, the most inexpensive tickets for the August 28th show in Wantagh are currently listed at $95 on Viagogo . Those hoping to catch The Who at Madison Square Garden on August 30th can find tickets starting at $112 on the same platform.
Fans are encouraged to explore multiple ticket marketplaces, including StubHub , Vivid Seats , TicketNetwork , and SeatGeek , to compare prices and potentially find even better deals. New customers to Vivid Seats can also take advantage of a $20 discount on orders over $200 by using the promo code NJ20 at checkout.
A Farewell Tour with Star Power
The Who launched “The Song Is Over Farewell Tour” on August 16 in Sunrise, Florida, and the tour is scheduled to conclude on September 28 in Las Vegas. Throughout the tour, a diverse lineup of supporting artists will share the stage with The Who on select dates, including Billy Bob Thornton and The Boxmasters, Billy Idol, Feist, Joe Bonamassa, and The Joe Perry Project.
Other NYC Concerts to Anticipate
The Who isn’t the only major act heading to New York in the coming months. Music fans can also look forward to performances by Dua Lipa, Kali Uchis, Ethel Cain, and HAIM.
“This definitely will be the last tour of the US, that’s for sure,” a representative for the band stated to Pollstar . “We will not be back touring.”
For those looking to relive hits like “Teenage Wasteland” one last time, securing tickets now is crucial. A complete schedule of The Who’s tour dates can be found [here]( insert link to tour schedule here ).
